title: Photo Palette — pull a crafting palette from any photo
description: Upload a photo, which is read in the browser and never sent anywhere, or use one of three scenes drawn in the page: a sunset, a Texas bluebonnet field, a desert. Extract 3 to 10 colours with seeded k-means in CIELAB or with median cut, see each colour's share of the picture, and get a name from a 40-colour list by nearest ΔE*ab. A WCAG contrast matrix and suggested AA text/background pairs come with it, plus yarn stripes, an Ohio-star quilt block and a nail-polish set that links to Nail Studio. Export as CSS variables or JSON, or copy a hex.
prompt: Make a photo palette tool for crafters. I upload a photo or use demo images drawn in the page (a sunset, a Texas bluebonnet field, a desert). Extract 3–10 colours with seeded k-means in CIELAB or median cut (a toggle) and show the proportions. Name the colours from a small built-in name list by nearest ΔE. Build a WCAG contrast matrix with suggested text/background pairs that pass AA. Add 'for your hobby' outputs: yarn stripes, a quilt block preview, and a nail-polish set that links to ../lab/133-nail-studio.html. Export as CSS variables or JSON, and copy HEX. Photos must never leave the browser. The spec should check extraction on a synthetic image with known colour areas (proportions within tolerance for both algorithms), the contrast ratios against the WCAG formula computed in the test, the nearest-name mapping, the exports' exact text and the upload flow.

methodology: Synthetic uploads: the test paints horizontal bands of known colours on a canvas (50/30/20 and 40/25/20/15 per cent), turns toDataURL into a Buffer and sets it on the file input. Both algorithms must return those exact colours (ΔE < 2) with shares within ±2 points, and asking for more colours than exist is reported rather than invented.

WCAG oracle: the test's own luminance and contrast code is checked against published values (21:1 for black on white, 4.54 for #767676 on white and just under 4.5 for #777777, 8.59 for blue, 4.0 for red), then compared with every cell of the matrix: raw ratio, two-decimal text, and AA / AA-large / fail level. Every suggested pair on all three demo scenes must reach 4.5.

Names: an independent sRGB → CIELAB (D65) conversion and ΔE*ab 1976 in the test picks the nearest of the page's 40 names for every colour of every demo, and exact list colours must come back with ΔE 0.
Exports are compared as literal strings: the full CSS block and the pretty-printed JSON for the known image are written out in the spec.

Privacy and flow: no request leaves the origin during an upload, the status says the file was read locally with its size, a text file is refused with an error and the previous palette is kept, and the privacy note sits next to the input.
risks: Downscaling blends neighbouring pixels, so photos gain in-between colours; synthetic images are kept under the 200-pixel analysis size so their colours stay exact.
Median cut can split a box between identical values; the page only cuts between different values, closest to the weighted median.
Colour-managed PNGs could shift values. The test's PNGs carry no colour profile, and the palette of an ordinary photo is approximate anyway.
The clipboard API needs permission and a secure context; the page falls back to execCommand and says so if both fail.
qa.playwright: setInputFiles with an in-memory buffer drives the real upload path (File → createImageBitmap → canvas) without fixture files, and because the PNG is drawn in the browser the expected colours are known exactly. context.grantPermissions(['clipboard-read', 'clipboard-write']) lets the test read back what Copy wrote, on both projects. One surprise, and it came from the test machine rather than the page: on Windows, reading the clipboard back returned the CSS with CRLF line endings, so the exact-text comparison failed. The test now normalises line endings for the clipboard check; the textarea export is still compared byte for byte. A second browser page from the same context confirms seeded demo scenes and k-means starts give identical palettes.
coverage: Upload flow: known colours and shares, local-only status, no requests
k-means and median cut on a four-colour image; too-large k
Contrast vs WCAG reference values and every matrix cell
Suggested AA pairs on three demos
Copy HEX / Copy CSS via the clipboard
Demo scenes, bluebonnet blue, seeded determinism, ?seed=
Yarn stripe rows, Ohio star colours, polish bottles + Nail Studio link

a11y: The file input has a visible label with the privacy note beside it, and the demo buttons use aria-pressed. The method toggle is a native radio group, and the colour count is a labelled range with a live output. Status messages, including errors, go to an aria-live region. Every swatch shows its name, hex and share as text, the proportion bar and hobby previews have descriptive aria-labels, the contrast matrix has row and column headers naming the colours, and each Copy button is labelled with the hex it copies.
